criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: Opens with the June 29 deadline, names the Fairbanks utility grid dependency, and ends the first paragraph with the unresolved who-pays question. Lands within the ~210-char see-more cutoff.

criteria.name: Industry relevance
criteria.notes: Every story localizes to Alaska with a sector consequence: GVEA cost allocation, HB 381 revenue impact, FERC regulatory contrast, NOAA compute-demand texture.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Specifics every 1-2 sentences: AFCEC-26-R-0006, June 29, three bases, 138-kV line, named officials and verbatim quotes, 34-5 vote, rule of 11, June 19 expiry, FERC vote, IFCB, AOOS.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Primary sources present (SAM.gov via HigherGov, AF.mil, NOAA, AOOS); validator-stripped figures stayed out. FERC vote is single-outlet (AP via ADN) and the rule of 11 is single-sourced to ADN, both attributed in body.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Position-taking, structural cost-allocation ternary, no banned phrases or influencer cadence. FERC paragraph reads slightly newswire.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Six tight paragraphs, ~448 words, ~2751 chars, under the 3000 cap. Paragraph 2 is proper-noun dense.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Names all three parties in the developed tension, debatable, no CTA softener.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: Concrete revisit triggers: grid-cost assumptions for June 29 bids, HB 381 risk to the cheap-power assumption, FERC Lower-48 precedent.
